'''Vector Gas Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline running from the United States to Canada.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2kKJiXQ Vector Gas Pipeline,] Wikipedia, accessed January 2018</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from Joliet, Illinois to Dawn, Ontario.<ref name="en" />

==Background==

=== Main Line ===
The Vector Pipeline is operated by Vector Pipeline L.P., which is owned by Enbridge (60%) and DTE Energy (40%).<ref name=freep>[https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/2015/02/03/natural-gas-pipeline-vector-rover-enbridge-dte/22813789/ Vector shelves pipeline expansion], Detroit Free Press, Feb. 3, 2015</ref> Vector sought permits from the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and Canada Energy Regulator in 1997. The pipeline began operation on Dec 01, 2000.<ref name="en" /> In October 2014, Vector Pipeline proposed expanding the pipeline with a 42-in. OD loop that would increase the pipeline's capacity to 1.3 bcfd, and modifying the pipeline so that gas could flow bidirectionally.<ref>[http://www.ogj.com/articles/2014/10/vector-pipeline-floats-doubling-capacity-bidirectional-flow.html Vector Pipeline floats doubling capacity, bidirectional flow], Oil & Gas Journal, Oct. 8, 2014</ref> In February 2015, it was reported that the plan to expand the pipeline and reverse the flow had been abandoned.<ref name=freep>[https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/2015/02/03/natural-gas-pipeline-vector-rover-enbridge-dte/22813789/ Vector shelves pipeline expansion], Detroit Free Press, Feb. 3, 2015</ref>

=== Blue Water Energy Center (BWEC) Pipeline ===
The expansion extends the Vector Pipeline to the Blue Water Energy Center, a 1,100 GW combined cycle power plant in St. Clair, MI owned by DTE Energy. The expansion pipeline can expand to 525 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d) of capacity with equipment upgrade.<ref name=":0" />

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, the construction of the project was completed in December 2021 and began service.<ref name=":0" />

=== Blue Water Compressor Project ===
The new compressor station expands capacity from 120,000 MMcf/d to 500,000 Mcf/d on its interconnect with the Vector Pipeline.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> The project involved adding a new 11,150 hp compressor station will be set up. The U.S. FERC issued clearance for the project in 2019.<ref name=":1" />

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, the construction of the project was completed in November 2021 and began service.<ref name=":0" />
